quizzes.title: Cauvery River and its basin: Practice MCQs
quizzes.passage: The Cauvery is a river at the centre of a long-running dispute among the states that share its waters. The dispute has historical roots in an agreement between the Madras Presidency and the princely state of Mysore. Madras objected when Mysore planned to expand irrigation and to construct water storage structures on the river. The river later became a major source of contention between the successor states. Karnataka is the upper riparian state, and it seeks greater water availability for drinking water in Bengaluru city and for irrigation. Tamil Nadu is the lower riparian state, and it seeks assured releases of water for agriculture in the Cauvery delta. To understand the dispute, it helps to know some basic facts about the river itself. The Cauvery's drainage basin is divided into an upper part and a lower part. Several major dams have been built on the river, and the states through which it passes share its waters. The dispute was taken up at the national level, where it was brought under the Constitution and a central law. A tribunal was later constituted to hear the dispute, and its award allocated water among the states concerned. Taken together, these facts show why the river has remained at the centre of the dispute.

quizzes.title: Cauvery River and its basin: Practice TITA
quizzes.passage: The conflict over the Cauvery is between states that share the river's water but depend on it for different purposes. Karnataka, the upper riparian state, has sought more water for drinking needs in its major city and for irrigation. Tamil Nadu, the lower riparian state, has sought dependable releases of water for farming in its delta. The roots of the dispute lie in an agreement reached between the Madras Presidency and the princely state of Mysore. Madras opposed Mysore's plans to widen irrigation and to build storage structures on the river. After the states became successor states, the issue continued to be a major source of contention. The matter was taken up under the Constitution and a central statute, and a tribunal was later constituted to settle the sharing of water. The river has several major dams, and its basin is divided into an upper part and a lower part. These details show why each state's claim follows from its position on the river, and why the dispute has lasted so long. The states' claims are therefore not abstract. Karnataka's position as the upper riparian state and Tamil Nadu's position as the lower riparian state each shape what the two governments ask for from the river, and each state's demands are set against the other's. Keeping these positions in mind makes the later facts about the river much easier to follow.

quizzes.title: Mekedatu project and the latest order: Practice MCQs
quizzes.passage: The Cauvery dispute is shaped by the positions of the states along the river. Karnataka lies upstream as the upper riparian state, while Tamil Nadu lies downstream as the lower riparian state. Karnataka has sought greater availability of water for its own needs, and Tamil Nadu has sought assured releases of water for agriculture in the Cauvery delta. The dispute has a long history, going back to an agreement of 1892 between the Madras Presidency and the princely state of Mysore. Madras objected when Mysore planned to expand irrigation and build storage structures on the river. In the present phase, two developments have drawn attention. A regulatory body on the river has endorsed an order concerning the release of water from Karnataka to Tamil Nadu. Separately, Karnataka has put forward the Mekedatu Balancing Reservoir Project on the Cauvery River. Projects of this kind can affect how much water flows downstream to the lower riparian state. The river also has several major dams, which are part of the water system the states share. The sections above describe the states' positions, the historical agreement, and the two developments that have drawn attention to the dispute. Taken together, these points show why any new step on the river is examined closely in relation to the flow of water to Tamil Nadu.
